content.text:
I'm now comparing the final and proposed rules for more differences, and I've noted a cross-reference in 351.503(a)(1) that points to a different paragraph (430.208(e) versus 430.208(d)), along with a label change from "Minimally Successful" to "Minimally Satisfactory" for Level 2. I'm also starting to look at 503(d), where the final version adds a clause that I haven't finished reading yet.

I'm going through the remaining differences: the final version adds language about patterns authorized under 430.208(d) in 503(d) and 503(e)(2), and a few wording tweaks appear in 351.503(b)(3) and 351.503(f)(2). The more substantive changes are 351.504(a), where "should" becomes "must," and 351.505(b)(2), where the cross-reference moves from 503(b) to 504(b), plus a possible shift in meaning in 351.506(c)(1) about whose performance credit and service computation dates are listed.

I'm checking the remaining proposed-versus-final differences, including a correction that seems to change a cross-reference in 351.506(c)(2) from "(b) and (c)" to just "(b)". I'm also noting that 351.506(d) now adds a clause about not limiting rights of access under other statutes or regulations. Next I'll move on to subparts F through H, reading that section compactly.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

content.text:
I'm noting that the 351.604 amendment from the proposed version doesn't appear in the final one, so that change was dropped. I'm also seeing that 351.605 was restructured: the wording of paragraph (a) changed, and the final version says the assignment rights "must not" apply where the proposed said "may not."

I'm checking the remaining cross-reference and heading changes in 351.606 through 351.702. The section 351.209(b) citation became 353.209(b), and 351.606(a) now also covers 351.605 alongside 351.601. In 351.608, the CTAP reference moved from subpart E to subpart F, and the 351.701 criteria now point explicitly to 351.702 and 351.703.

I'm checking the new exemption in 351.702(a)(4)(v) against Silva's case: he held the same position until 2023 with a Level 4 rating in 2022, which falls inside the five-year window ending on the notice date. That would exempt him from the assessment, though he would still need to meet the qualification requirements in 351.702(a)(1)–(3). I'm now turning to the self-rating questionnaire, which is scored automatically and may not comply with 351.702(a)(4).

I'm checking the remaining provisions in 351.802 and 351.805 in the proposed version, and I plan to read that stretch of the text next.

I'm comparing the proposed and final versions of 351.802: "veteran status" became "veterans' preference subgroup," and item (3) now points to 5 CFR part 351 and explains how to access the agency's records instead of just naming them. The final rule also adds a new 351.805(b) with no recalculation, and an introductory paragraph to (a) that the proposal lacked. For part 353, the proposal had no 353.209 at all.

I'm checking the preamble against the regulation text for Q13, and the tenure group descriptions in both look consistent so far. Next I'll search the preamble for the specific section references and time limits like 351.605, 351.606, 90 days, and 60 days.

I'm going to scan the Exec Summary (lines 93–255) for how the rule's provisions are summarized, since it should give me a cleaner read on the Q13 mismatch than grepping for individual time limits.

content.text:
I'm comparing the preamble's wording on 351.402(c) against the rule text, and the preamble says OPM "review" where the text requires "approval." I'm checking whether the other competitive-area wording lines up too.

I'm checking the Tulsa notices against the 90-day rule: designated August 17 and noticed October 13 is 57 days, so OPM approval in advance was required and nothing was sent. I'm also noting that the "access" wording in the 5 CFR part 351 passage doesn't match the "information on how to access" language in the text.

I'm going through the remaining wording checks against the rule text, including the 351.608(f) military spouse limit, the 351.506 and 351.805 cross-references, and the tenure group definition, which look consistent with the text.

I've gone through the remaining mismatch checks: the exec summary points on abolishing positions within 180 days, the emergency shutdown furlough definition, and the 90-day competitive area trigger all look consistent with the text. Now I'm turning to the exceptions and temporary discussion around lines 2929-3012, including the USERRA passage and its "6-month or 1-year" wording.

I'm now checking the Subpart B discussion on 351.202(d), around lines 1544 to 2090, for a mismatch on temporary appointments, so I'll search the preamble for "subpart C" and "term."

content.text:
I've found something important in Q13: the preamble on page 49190 describes erosion of duties as an agency having formally announced a RIF in a competitive area, with the RIF taking effect within 180 days. The regulatory text in 351.202(c)(3), though, covers the period between the announcement and the completion of the RIF, with no 180-day limit. So the two don't match, and I need to check the surrounding lines to see which one governs.

I'm checking the preamble's 180-day wording against the regulatory text, which has no such limit. I want to read the surrounding lines to see which version governs, and I also need to confirm that the probationary exemption and Ortiz's case line up with the rule.

I'm working through the remaining Q9 steps and the notice requirements, checking each one against the 351.608 and 351.802 rules. Then I'm starting to look at the Jordan GS-13 case and its rights to positions.

3. Erosion-of-duties paragraph. Preamble at 91 FR 49190 says OPM 'is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove' erosion-of-duties reclassifications. The reclassification exemption and its safeguard are in 351.202(c)(3) (91 FR 49218), whereas 351.201(a)(2) just lists the actions covered. The preamble's description of the safeguard elsewhere on the same page (bars reclassification 'between the formal announcement and completion of a RIF', 91 FR 49190, and Exec. Summary item 8 at 49178) matches the text; the 180-day language at 49190 describes the old rule's trigger.
4. Notice content on records access. Preamble at 91 FR 49205 and 49191 says notices must give 'a link to 5 CFR part 351 and access to the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force'. Text, 351.802(a)(3) (49226): 'A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force'. Items 1 and 2 are drawn from separate summary sentences; the regulatory text controls."},"Q14":{"answer":"All items below are checked against the cited text. The final appeals rule is 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230), as corrected by 2026-17338; the proposal is 2026-02576 (91 FR 5861, text at 5874-77); the Board's rule is 2026-16456 (91 FR 51997).
(i) Preamble v. regulatory text (published or corrected):
1. 351.901(b)(1). Preamble (91 FR 49248): the appellant must prove 'that the written appeal was timely and in the required form'. Text (49263): 'The timeliness of the written appeal', with nothing about form.
2. 351.901(c)(1). Preamble (49248): 'the procedures in part 351 are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action'. Text as published (49263): 'The procedures in this part'; as corrected by 2026-17338: 'The procedures in this subpart'.
3. Existing collective bargaining agreements. Preamble (91 FR 49244-45): the rule 'does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs', does not 'automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term', and 'when agreements are renegotiated' the rule will limit the duty and ability to bargain. Text 351.901(c)(2) (49263-64): RIF actions and appeal matters 'may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration', for covered RIFs from Sept. 2, with no renegotiation condition.
4. Judicial review. Preamble (91 FR 49242-43): the rule 'does not withdraw judicial review that Congress provided'. Text 351.901(c)(4) (49264): 'A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart'; 351.909(e): no further right of appeal.
5. 351.904(c). Preamble (49250) says 'OPM or the responsible agency may disallow'. As corrected, the text says 'the agency whose action is under appeal', because 'responsible agency' is undefined in part 351.
(ii) Changes from proposal to final not acknowledged in the final rule's summary of changes (91 FR 49230-32):
1. 351.901(c)(3): the proposal listed the Federal Labor Relations Authority among the entities whose matters are preserved (5874-75); the final drops FLRA (49264). The summary lists EEOC, IGs, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC without saying FLRA was removed.
2. 351.903(b)(1): the proposal said the agency response is due 'within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal' (5875); the final says 'within 30 calendar days after service of the initial appeal' (49264).
3. 351.905(c): the proposal allowed 'a hearing or any other appropriate action' and directed the parties to participate (5876); the final keeps only 'a hearing' (49265-66). The final also adds OPM's power to 'require either party to provide additional information'.
4. 351.902(c)(2): the final adds 'or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause' to the registration requirement (49264).
5. 351.906(b): the proposal said OPM 'shall' impose the listed sanctions (5876); the final says 'may' (49266). The final also adds (c), requiring sanctions to be proportionate and no broader than necessary.
6. 351.909(c): the final adds that an untimely request granted for good cause leads to a decision that becomes final under (b) (49266-67). The authority citation is also expanded (1103, 1104, 2301, 38 U.S.C. 4331).
(iii) The Board's rule (2026-16456) v. OPM's rule and within itself, on which RIF appeals the Board will still hear:
1. Within the Board's rule: DATES (91 FR 51997) says the Board will not apply the rule to pending cases or 'newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken before the effective date'. These use three different tests: action date, notice date and RIF effective date.

The Board's Section III test (effective date before Sept. 2) would leave a RIF with notice before Sept. 2 and an effective date on or after Sept. 2 (for example, notice Aug. 31, effective Oct. 30) outside both OPM's process and the Board's stated rule. Q1.answer:
(a) The final rule is 'Reduction in Force', FR Doc. 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178-49227. It was published Aug. 3, 2026 and is effective Sept. 2, 2026. Docket OPM-2025-0107; RIN 3206-AO86.
(b) The proposed rule is 'Reduction in Force', FR Doc. 2026-04377, published Mar. 5, 2026, beginning at 91 FR 10904 (same docket and RIN). I did not confirm its end page.
(c) Two corrections to the main rule have been published.
- 2026-17335, 91 FR 54794-96, published Aug. 25, 2026, effective Sept. 2, 2026. It corrects typographical and clerical errors in parts 316, 330, 351, 353 and 430. These include amendatory instructions 15, 36 and 39, 'of this part' references to 11.2 and 11.3 (now 'of this chapter'), list structure in 351.702(a)(4)(iv), and added part 316 fixes. It also conforms the part 351 authority citation to the appeals rule (adds 5 U.S.C. 1103 and 1104), and makes cross-reference fixes in 351.402, 351.503, 351.506(c)(2), 351.606 and 430.208(e)(4). Its docket line reads OPM-2026-0107, which differs from the rule's OPM-2025-0107.
- 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363-64, published Sept. 15, 2026, effective Sept. 15, 2026. It restores paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) of the definition of 'displaced' in 5 CFR 330.602. Instruction 11 of the main rule had inadvertently removed them.
(There is also 2026-17338, but it corrects the separate appeals rule 2026-15666, not this rule.)
(d) RIFs for which the agency issues the specific RIF notice on or after Sept. 2, 2026 are governed by part 351 as amended. RIFs for which notice was issued before Sept. 2, 2026 are processed under the regulations in effect when the notice was issued. This is stated in the DATES paragraph of 2026-15665 (91 FR 49178) and in Section IV 'Implementation Considerations' (91 FR 49206-07). The appeals rule 2026-15666 has its own, matching trigger in its DATES paragraph (91 FR 49230): it applies only to RIF actions for which the specific notice under 351.802 issued on or after Sept. 2, 2026.
(e) Other 2026 final rules that amend part 351 on or after Sept. 2, 2026:
- 2026-15666 (RIF Appeals, 91 FR 49230). It revises the part 351 authority citation and 351.802(a)(6) (right to appeal to OPM, time limit, e-filing system). It also revises 351.807(e) and replaces all of subpart I (351.901-909: OPM replaces MSPB as the appeal forum). Effective Sept. 2, 2026. It is in force today, but only for notices issued on or after Sept. 2.
- 2026-21320 (Administrative Leave, 91 FR 65924). It revises 351.806 (status during the notice period) and the authority citation. Effective Nov. 18, 2026. Not yet in force today (Nov. 14).
- 2026-21316 (Managing Senior Professional Performance, 91 FR 65904). It amends 351.203 (definition of 'Rating of record', updated to 430.208(e) and part 430 subpart E). The authority citation 'continues to read' as already amended. Effective Nov. 18, 2026. Not yet in force today.
Excluded: 2026-13715 (91 FR 41521) is effective Aug. 6, 2026, before the main rule, and only updated cross-references in the old 351.504. My search with a part 351 filter found no other 2026 final rules touching part 351.
Q1.basis: fr_doc and text of 2026-15665 (DATES; Sec. IV at 91 FR 49206-07); 2026-17335; 2026-18800; 2026-15666 (DATES, instructions 1-4); 2026-21320 (91 FR 65939); 2026-21316 (91 FR 65914-16); search results for 5 CFR 351 filter and OPM rules; 2026-04377 (metadata).
Q1.uncertainty: I did not confirm the end page of the proposed rule. The part 351 CFR filter might miss a rule that amends part 351 without being indexed to it (I found none). 2026-13715 was excluded on the effective-date criterion.

Q2.answer:
Notices were issued Sept. 3, 2026, which is on or after Sept. 2, so amended part 351 applies. The ratings period is Sept. 3, 2022 to Sept. 3, 2026 and all ratings listed fall inside it. Values: Level 5 = 7, Level 4 = 5, Level 3 = 3, Levels 1-2 = 0 (351.503(a)).
(a) Performance credit + veterans' points = total:
- Abbott: 7+5+5 = 17; no preference, 0; total 17.
- Bianchi: 5+0+3 = 8; a 30% disabled preference eligible gets +5 (351.504(a)(1), Subgroup AD); total 13.
- Castillo: 7+5+5 = 17. He is a retired member, so 351.504(b) applies. Not (b)(1), because the retirement is not disability-based. Not (b)(2), because the retired pay is based on 22 years (20 or more). Not (b)(3). So he is not a preference eligible: 0 points, Subgroup B; total 17.
- Dalton: only two ratings, so the proxy is (7+0)/2 = 3.5 (351.503(f)(2)). Credit = 7+0+3.5 = 10.5; +3 (351.504(a)(2), Subgroup A) = 13.5.
- Eze: 5+5+5 = 15; 0; total 15. A term appointee who is not career and has finished any probationary or trial period is in competitive tenure subgroup II (351.502(a)(3)). He is in the same tenure group as the others.
- Fontaine: one rating, so 5 x 3 = 15 (351.503(f)(3)); 0; total 15.
(b) Order of retention (351.501): first by tenure group, then by total in descending order, then ties by tenure subgroup (I before II), then earliest SCD.
1. Abbott, 17.
2. Castillo, 17. The tie with Abbott is broken by SCD: Abbott's May 1, 2003 is earlier than Castillo's Aug. 1, 2012. Both are subgroup I.
3. Fontaine, 15.
4. Eze, 15. The tie is broken by tenure subgroup, not SCD: Fontaine is in subgroup I and Eze in subgroup II, so Fontaine ranks ahead despite Eze's earlier SCD (2009).
5. Dalton, 13.5.
6. Bianchi, 13.
The two released are Bianchi and Dalton, the lowest two. Dalton's veterans' points and Bianchi's AD points do not lift them above 15.
(c) Under the earlier rules, as the preamble describes them, employees were ranked by tenure group, then veterans' subgroup (AD, A, B), and only then by adjusted SCD (SCD moved back by performance years: 20 for Level 5, 16 for Level 4, 12 for Level 3, averaged and rounded). Bianchi (subgroup AD) would therefore have ranked above Abbott (subgroup B) in tenure group I regardless of performance or service. Under the 2026 rule she ranks below him (13 v. 17).
(d) 351.506(c) entitles an employee who has received a specific notice to review the complete retention register for her competitive level. This includes the names of all employees on it, each one's performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, and each one's SCD, so she can see how the level was constructed and how standing was determined. She may also review the complete registers for other positions that could affect the composition of her level or her assignment rights (351.506(c)(2)). Under 351.506(b) she or her representative may inspect the registers and related records. Disclosure is subject to FOIA and the Privacy Act (351.506(e)). The text does not say that the register lists each employee's individual ratings. Her own notice must state her three most recent ratings (351.802(a)(2)).
Q2.uncertainty: The text of the earlier rules is not printed in the documents; part (c) rests on the preamble's description. Eze's competitive-service status is inferred from the term appointment. If he were excepted service he would be on a separate register (351.501(a)). The definition of 'modal rating' is not printed (not needed here).

Q3.answer:
(a) The relevant text is 351.504(a)-(b), under which a retired member is a preference eligible only if (b)(1), (b)(2) or (b)(3) is met. (b)(4) and (b)(5) only limit that further for majors and above.
- A: Not a preference eligible. 22 years' service so (b)(2) fails; no disability retirement so (b)(1) fails; (b)(3) fails. 0 points, Subgroup B (351.504(a)(3)).
- B: Not a preference eligible. His retired pay is based on 21 years and his disability is not the basis of retirement. 0 points, Subgroup B. Being 40% disabled does not help, because (b)(4) still requires one of (b)(1)-(3), and none is met.
- C: A preference eligible under (b)(1)(i) (disability retirement from injury in armed conflict) and also (b)(2) (14 years). As a major she also needs (b)(4): she is a disabled veteran under 5 U.S.C. 2108(2) and meets (b)(1)/(b)(2). With 60% compensable disability she gets +5 and is in Subgroup AD (351.504(a)(1)). (b)(5) does not apply on the facts; nothing says she retired under 10 U.S.C. chapter 67.
- D: Not a preference eligible (24 years, no disability). 0 points, Subgroup B.
- E: Staff sergeant, so (b)(4) does not apply. A preference eligible under (b)(2): the medical retirement at 16 years is not based on 20 or more years. 10% disability is under 30%, so +3 and Subgroup A (351.504(a)(2)).
(b) Under 351.505(b)(2) a retired member covered by 351.504(b) gets credit only for (i) active service during a war or in a campaign or expedition with an authorized badge, or (ii) all active service if he is a preference eligible under 351.504(b). Under 351.505(d)(2) the SCD is the most recent appointment date minus total creditable service.
- A is not a preference eligible, so only the 2 campaign-badge years count: Sept. 7, 2010 minus 2 years = Sept. 7, 2008. His other 20 years do not count.
- C is a preference eligible, so all 14 active years count: Sept. 7, 2010 minus 14 years = Sept. 7, 1996.
(c) The veterans' preference subgroups AD, A and B are labels that must be shown on the retention register (351.504(a)) and in the notice (351.802(a)(2)). They do not rank anyone. Retention order is by tenure group, then performance credit augmented by the 5, 3 or 0 points, then tenure subgroup, then SCD (351.501). The text does not use AD/A/B as a separate tie-breaker.
Q3.uncertainty: Whether C and the (b)(5) age-60 rule interact depends on whether C's retired pay falls under 10 U.S.C. chapter 67, which the scenario does not say. The definition of 'disabled veteran' in 5 U.S.C. 2108(2) is statutory and not printed in the Federal Register documents. I treated C's 60% compensable rating as meeting it.

Q4.answer:
Notices were issued Sept. 3, 2026, so amended 351.503 applies. The four-year period before the notices runs from Sept. 3, 2022.
(a) With no cutoff, the three most recent ratings of record received in the period are Aug. 10, 2026 (Level 5 = 7), Nov. 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3) and Nov. 15, 2024 (Level 3 = 3). Credit = 7+3+3 = 13 (351.503(a),(c)(1)).
(b) The cutoff date is Sept. 3, 2026 minus 45 days = July 20, 2026 (Sept. 3 less 3 days is Aug. 31; less 31 more is July 31; less 11 more is July 20). The Aug. 10, 2026 rating was put on record after the cutoff and cannot be used (351.503(c)(2)). The four-year period is then July 20, 2022 to July 20, 2026. The three most recent ratings are Nov. 14, 2025 (3), Nov. 15, 2024 (3) and Nov. 20, 2023 (Level 4 = 5). Credit = 3+3+5 = 11.
(c) On the text, no. 351.503(c)(2) says that after the cutoff no new ratings of record 'will be put on record and used'. 351.503(c)(3) requires that a rating both be issued with all reviews and signatures and be 'on record', meaning available to the office that builds the registers. This rating was given July 15 (before the cutoff) but not on record until Aug. 15 (after it), so it is not usable. (The scenario's general assumption that a rating is on record the day it is received does not apply here.) 351.503(c)(4)(i) lets the agency define in its issuances when a rating is 'received'. Within that agency discretion, put-on-record is the test the text states.
(d) Gina's Aug. 15, 2022 Level 5 is before Sept. 3, 2022, so it falls outside the four years. She has two ratings: Level 4 (5) and Level 3 (3). The proxy is (5+3)/2 = 4. Credit = 5+3+4 = 12 (351.503(f)(2)).
(e) With no rating of record in the period, 351.503(f)(1) bases credit on 'the modal rating as defined in 351.203' for the pattern that applies to his position. The documents do not print that definition or say what the modal level is for a five-level pattern, so I cannot give a number from the Federal Register. The most defensible reading is that he gets the modal rating's point value; if the modal level is Level 3 that is 9 (3 x 3), but that is not verified.
Q4.uncertainty: The definition of 'modal rating' is existing 351.203 text that no document prints, so (e) cannot be answered with certainty. In (c), the interaction with the agency's own 'received' definition under 351.503(c)(4) is an inference.

Q5.answer:
(a) The earlier rules apply to notices issued before Sept. 2, 2026; the amended rules apply to notices on or after Sept. 2 (DATES of 2026-15665).
(i) Notice Aug. 28 means the earlier rules apply. As the preamble describes them (91 FR 49186, 49198), employees are ranked by tenure group, then veterans' subgroup, then adjusted SCD, with extra service credit added back: 20 years for Level 5, 16 for Level 4, 12 for Level 3, averaged and rounded.
- Lee: Level 3/3/3 gives +12 years. Adjusted SCD = March 2, 1998 minus 12 years = March 2, 1986.
- Park: Level 5/5/5 gives +20 years. Adjusted SCD = July 8, 2019 minus 20 years = July 8, 1999.
Both are career employees in the same tenure group and in veterans' subgroup B, so the earliest adjusted SCD ranks higher. Lee (1986) outranks Park (1999) and Park is released. This matches the preamble's own example (Employee A 3/3/3, 1996 SCD, outranks Employee B 5/5/5, 2021 SCD).
(ii) Notice Sept. 2 is on the effective date, so the new rules apply. Lee: 3+3+3 = 9. Park: 7+7+7 = 21. No veterans' points. Park ranks higher and Lee is released.
(iii) Notice Sept. 3 gives the same result as (ii): Lee 9, Park 21, Lee released.
(b) No. Under 351.507(a), retention standing is determined as of the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice. Under 351.805(b), an amended notice issued solely to state a later effective date 'is not a new specific reduction in force notice' for 351.507 and does not require the agency to redetermine or recalculate standing. The Oct. 15 Level 5 for Lee was received after the Sept. 3 notice and is outside the ratings period (which ends at the notice date), so it is not used. Lee stays at 9 and Park at 21.
(c) The three events are:
- Which version of the rules applies: the date the agency issues the RIF notice (DATES and Sec. IV of 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178, 49206-07).
- End of the four-year ratings period: the date of issuance of the RIF notices, or the agency's cutoff date if it uses one (351.503(c)(1)-(2)).
- Tenure subgroup and retention standing: the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice (351.502(a)(2)-(3) and (b); 351.507(a)).
Q5.uncertainty: The earlier rules' text is not printed, so (a)(i) relies on the preamble's description (including 'averaged, rounded'). Lee and Park each have identical ratings, so no rounding issue arises.

Q6.answer:
Under 351.701(a), a released competitive-service employee with a current rating of record of Level 2 or higher must be offered assignment to a competitive position that requires no reduction, or the least reduction, in representative rate. The position must be in the same competitive area, have the same type of work schedule and be one he is qualified for. Under 351.701(b), it must be held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group and be no more than three grades (or grade intervals) below his own. The limit is five grades for a preference eligible with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more.
(a) Jordan, a GS-13 in one-grade interval progression with a Level 2 rating, has assignment rights to:
- position 1 (GS-12, Ellis);
- position 2 (GS-11, Frank);
- position 3 (GS-10, Gale).
The agency must offer position 1, the GS-12 held by Ellis, which is the least possible reduction.
The others are not available:
- Position 4 (GS-9, Hana) is four grades down, beyond the three-grade limit.
- Position 5 (Ito) is held by someone with higher standing.
- Position 6 (Kim) is part-time and does not match his full-time schedule.
- Position 7 (Lund) is in a different competitive area.
(b) Preference eligible with 30%+ disability: the limit becomes five grades, so position 4 (GS-9, Hana) also becomes an assignment right. The offer is still position 1 (GS-12, Ellis). Positions 5, 6 and 7 stay unavailable.
(c) Level 1: 351.701(a) requires a current rating of Level 2 or higher, so he has no assignment rights to any of the seven positions. This is the text's gap-free reading; it does not itself say what happens next beyond 'rather than furlough or separation' no longer being required.
(d) Excepted service: 351.701 applies to a 'competitive service tenure group employee'. 351.705(a) says an agency 'may, at its discretion, adopt provisions' giving excepted-service employees assignment rights under the same appointing authority on the same basis as 351.701. So there is no assignment right as a matter of the regulation. Any right depends on an agency policy the documents do not show.
(e) The 2026 text contains no rule that a Level 2 employee cannot take a position held by a higher-rated person. The only conditions are the released employee's current rating of Level 2 or higher (351.701(a)) and the holder's lower retention standing in the same tenure group (351.701(b)(1)). The text uses only 'assignment' and 'displacing'; it has no 'bumping' or 'retreating' categories. The preamble says the rule replaces 'bump and retreat' concepts with assignment to a position held by a lower-standing employee (91 FR 49178-79, item 12) and eliminates multiple rounds of bump and retreat (91 FR 49198).
Q6.basis: 2026-15665: 351.701(a)-(d), 351.705(a) (91 FR 49225-26); Exec. Summary item 12 (49178-79); preamble at 49198. 351.702-.703 qualifications were not reread; the scenario says Jordan is qualified.
Q6.uncertainty: 351.703 is not printed in these documents. Position 1: the text says 'least possible reduction' but does not address ties between equal-grade holders. Part (c): the documents do not describe what happens to a Level 1 employee beyond the absence of assignment rights.

Q7.answer:
(a) The Merit Systems Protection Board hears her appeal. Her notice (Aug. 31) was issued before Sept. 2, 2026, so OPM's new appeal process does not apply. 2026-15666 (DATES, 91 FR 49230) applies 'only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice ... on or after September 2, 2026', and 91 FR 49248 says earlier-notice RIF appeals 'continue to be adjudicated by the MSPB'. The main RIF rule 2026-15665 has the same notice-date trigger (91 FR 49178, 49206-07). The MSPB rule 2026-16456 (91 FR 51997) says MSPB will 'continue to adjudicate RIF appeals ... because the RIF actions were taken before the rule's effective date' and 'will accept such cases for filing where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date'. But its DATES and Sec. III instead speak of actions taken before Sept. 2 and of RIF 'effective date' preceding Sept. 2. Her Oct. 30 effective date is after Sept. 2, so those passages are inconsistent with the notice-date passages (see Q14(iii)). Documents bearing: 2026-15666 (DATES; 49248), 2026-15665 (DATES; Sec. IV), 2026-16456 and the correction 2026-17338 (not on this point).
(b) OPM hears the appeal (351.901(a)), because the notice was issued on or after Sept. 2. She must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website (351.902(a)); OPM does not accept email or postal filings absent good cause and approval. The appeal is due within 30 calendar days from the effective date (351.902(b)), by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the 30th calendar day, with the first day counted being the day after the effective date (351.902(b)(1)). Dec. 18, 2026 is day 0; Dec. 19 is day 1; Dec. 31 is day 13; Jan. 17, 2027 is day 30. Jan. 17, 2027 is a Sunday and Monday Jan. 18, 2027 is Martin Luther King Jr. Day (third Monday of January), a Federal holiday. The period therefore runs to the first workday after, Tuesday, Jan. 19, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.
(c) She bears the burden by a preponderance of the evidence (351.901(b)) to show (1) timeliness of the written appeal, (2) OPM jurisdiction, (3) the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM RIF regulation under part 351, and (4) the failure prejudiced her by causing the action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome. She has no entitlement to a hearing. Review is on the written record unless OPM determines a hearing is 'necessary and efficient' (record insufficiently developed on a material fact, or a material credibility dispute) (351.905(c); 91 FR 49239 says hearings are not barred).
(d) 351.901(c)(1)-(2): the subpart I procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action, and a RIF action and matters relating to its appeal 'may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration'. The text has no carve-out for existing agreements. The preamble (91 FR 49244-45) says the final rule 'does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs', does not 'automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term', and that 'when agreements are renegotiated' the rule will limit agencies' duty and ability to bargain for a direct RIF appeal process. Questions about particular existing provisions are left to negotiability and unfair-labor-practice processes. The text itself is not conditioned on renegotiation (see Q14(i)).
(e) No on the text. 351.901(c)(4) says 'A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart', and 351.909(e) says there is no further right of appeal of an OPM final decision. The preamble (91 FR 49242-43) says the rule does not withdraw review Congress provided, but the regulatory text is controlling. Collateral matters within the independent jurisdiction of EEOC, an IG, MSPB, DOL VETS or OSC are preserved by 351.901(c)(3).
(f) Yes. 351.902(b)(3) lets an employee who timely filed a collateral matter within an entity's independent jurisdiction (OSC is listed in 351.901(c)(3)) file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision on that matter becomes final and no longer subject to further administrative review, if it materially affects her retention standing, order of release, assignment rights or other part 351 rights. OPM decides, in its sole and exclusive discretion, whether it does (the preamble uses a corrected-rating example, 91 FR 49249). March 10, 2027 plus 30 days is Friday, April 9, 2027 (21 days to Mar. 31, plus 9), at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. This assumes the March 10 decision is final and not further reviewable, and that counting starts the next day as in 351.902(b)(1).
(g) The applicability provision is the DATES paragraph of 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230), restated in the section-by-section analysis at 91 FR 49248, which notes that the regulatory text has no separate applicability note in 351.901. The main rule's DATES paragraph (91 FR 49178) and Sec. IV (91 FR 49206-07) give the same notice-date rule for the part 351 amendments.
Q7.uncertainty: Part (a): MSPB's own rule is internally inconsistent on whether the trigger is notice date or RIF effective date; the most defensible answer is MSPB (OPM's rule excludes pre-Sept. 2 notices; MSPB's notice-based passage accepts them), but the MSPB's effective-date passages would point the other way. The pre-Sept. 2 MSPB appeal rules themselves (former 351.901) are not printed. Part (f): whether OPM treats the OSC decision as materially affecting her rights is within OPM's discretion.

Q8.answer:
(a) The current text of 351.806 is not printed in any Federal Register document I could read. The adopting rule's preamble says current paragraph (a) uses the words 'when possible' for remaining in a duty status during the notice period (2026-21320, 91 FR 65926, 65933), and that 351.806(c) is a longstanding emergency provision. The adopted but not yet effective text is in 2026-21320 (91 FR 65924, 65939), effective Nov. 18, 2026:
- (a) 'Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period.'
- (b) 'Nothing in this section precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines that such leave is appropriate and the use of administrative leave is consistent with part 630, subpart N.'
- (c) In an emergency lack of work or funds, annual leave with or without consent, leave without pay with consent, or nonpay status without consent.
Today is Nov. 14, so this is adopted but not in force.
(b) Consent is not required for administrative leave. 351.806(b) and the companion provision 5 CFR 630.1403(c)(10) (added by the same rule) let the agency provide it 'when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests'. Consent appears only for leave without pay in 351.806(c). The preamble (91 FR 65933) says 'grant' wrongly implied administrative leave is given only on request, which 'has never been the case'. No fixed limit appears in 351.806(b) or 630.1403(c)(10). The new 630.1403(a)(3) says administrative leave is generally for brief periods (usually not more than 1 workday) but longer uses may be approved in the circumstances of paragraph (c). The preamble says that beginning in calendar year 2026 administrative leave in connection with a workforce realignment initiative is limited to 12 weeks in any individual instance unless OPM and OMB jointly approve a higher threshold (91 FR 65926). That sentence is preamble, and is made in the context of voluntary programs. The 10-workday statutory cap applies to investigative leave. A 60-day notice period (Oct. 19-Dec. 18) is about 8.6 weeks.
(c) OPM says its policy guidance (the 'Template for Agency Administrative Leave Policies', CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025, section D.1.b) 'already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee's receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of that separation', and that revised 351.806 is 'consistent with' it (91 FR 65926). OPM also says the 2025 programs were undertaken under existing regulatory authority and guidance (65926).
(d) No. OPM states that the revision addresses only whether an employee may be placed in a paid non-duty status; it does not alter RIF requirements and 'nothing in this rule authorizes an agency to bypass RIF competition, retention registers, or appeal rights' (65926). Retention standing is fixed at the date of the specific notice (351.507(a)), unaffected by leave status. Notice content is governed by 351.802. Appeal rights under subpart I run from the effective date of the action (351.902(b)).
Q8.uncertainty: The text of 351.806 and 630.1403 now in force (before Nov. 18) is not printed, so what the rules said on Oct. 26 can only be inferred from the preamble and guidance description. Whether the 12-week statement binds in this RIF context is not stated in regulatory text.

Q9.answer:
Notices were issued Oct. 13, 2026, after Sept. 2, so the amended rules (2026-15665) and the appeals rule (2026-15666) govern. Step by step:
1. Does not comply. 351.402(c): an agency that establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific notices must submit a description and a written statement of the bona fide organizational basis to OPM 'for approval in advance'. Aug. 17 to Oct. 13 is 57 days, so approval was required and nothing was sent. The step is otherwise consistent with 351.402(b)(1): the unit is on the official chart and approved by a designee, which is permitted so long as the designation is not delegated below headquarters level (the facts do not say).
2. In order. A career-conditional employee in an initial probationary period is not a 'competing employee' (351.202(d)(2)(ii)). The agency may retain her while releasing a competing employee (351.202(d)(3)).
3. Does not comply. 'Initial probationary period' excludes the supervisory or managerial probationary period (351.203). Ortiz has career tenure and is in subgroup I (351.502(a)(2)). She is a competing employee and must be ranked on the register (351.501).
4. Does not comply. A cutoff 30 days before Oct. 13 is Sept. 13, 2026. After the cutoff 'no new ratings of record will be put on record and used' (351.503(c)(2)); the Oct. 2 rating cannot be used, and ratings must be applied uniformly in the competitive area (351.503(c)(4)).
5. Does not comply. With two ratings the proxy is (7+5)/2 = 6, so credit = 7+5+6 = 18, not 15 (351.503(f)(2)). There is no 'presumed Level 3'.
6. Does not comply. For a single five-level pattern, 351.503(d) allows extra performance points only for systems whose highest summary level is Level 3 (pattern A or D). 351.503(e) concerns multiple patterns. Neither allows +2 for QSI recipients under a five-level pattern.
7. In order. 351.601(c): when employees have identical performance credit (with veterans' points), the same tenure subgroup and identical service dates, 'the agency may select any tied employee for release'.
8. Does not comply. 351.602(a): an agency may not release a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Reyes's promotion ends in March 2027.
9. In order. 351.702(a)(4)(v) excuses the assessment if during the 5 years ending on the notice date (Oct. 13, 2021 to Oct. 13, 2026) the employee occupied the same position (or a same grade/duties one) and received Level 3 or higher. Silva held it until 2023 and was rated Level 4 in 2022. The other 351.701 and 351.702 conditions still apply.
10. Does not comply. 351.702(a)(4) requires an assessment that allows demonstration of job-related skills, is based on a job analysis and 'does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment'.
11. Does not comply. 351.608(b) allows up to 90 days for undue interruption, but 351.608(a)(3) says each exception stands alone and may not be 'sequenced or stacked'. An exception over 30 days also requires written notice to higher-standing employees and a register entry (351.608(a)(4)). The agency may apply the single exception giving the longest retention.
12. Does not comply. For notices on or after Sept. 2, 351.802(a)(6) (as amended by 2026-15666) requires the notice to state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b) (30 calendar days from the effective date, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time) and the electronic filing system on OPM's website. The notice names MSPB and gives a different time basis ('within 30 days after it takes effect' is close to the OPM count but the forum is wrong).
Q9.uncertainty: Step 1: whether the designee satisfies the headquarters-level requirement is not stated. Step 9: the facts do not say whether the lower-grade position is one he held or one with the same grade and duties; the five-year test covers either. Step 12: the notice's 30-day period matches the OPM time limit; the defect is the forum and missing e-filing information.

Q10.answer:
(a) On Sept. 10, 2026, paragraph (1) of the definition of 'displaced' in 5 CFR 330.602 consisted only of the introductory text as revised by the Reduction in Force final rule (2026-15665, instruction 11, effective Sept. 2): 'A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:' with no sub-paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii). The reason is that instruction 11 revised paragraph (1) and set out only its introductory text, which, per OPM, 'inadvertently resulted in the removal' of (1)(i) (receipt of a RIF separation notice) and (1)(ii) (proposed removal under part 752 for declining a directed geographic relocation) (2026-18800, 91 FR 58363).
(b) 2026-18800, a correcting amendment published Sept. 15, 2026 (91 FR 58363-64) and effective Sept. 15, 2026, revised paragraph (1) in its entirety and restored (1)(i) and (1)(ii). OPM found good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) to issue it without notice and comment because the document 'makes no substantive change', restores text in effect before Sept. 2 that OPM did not propose to remove and that the final rule did not discuss removing, so notice and comment were unnecessary. It found good cause under 553(d)(3) for immediate effect on the same grounds. OPM characterized it as a correction restoring omitted text, not a change.
(c) Restored (1)(i) covers an employee who received a RIF separation notice 'and has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated'. A lower-rate offer is not such an offer, so declining it does not remove 'displaced' status under (1)(i); Nadia remains displaced. If the offered full-time position had the same representative rate, then declining it means she has declined a qualifying offer and is no longer displaced under (1)(i).
Q10.basis: 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363-64); 2026-15665 instruction 11 as described there (91 FR 49217).
Q10.uncertainty: I did not reread instruction 11 itself; I relied on 2026-18800's description of it. Whether Nadia would qualify as displaced under another paragraph, or by an offer's acceptance, is outside the question.

Q11.answer:
Differences in the part 351 regulatory text, proposed (2026-04377, 91 FR 10926-34) v. final (2026-15665, 91 FR 49218-26), as published. Where the 2026-17335 correction later changed the final text, I note it.
1. Authority citation: proposed 5 U.S.C. 1302, 3502, 3503; final adds 2301 and 38 U.S.C. 4331 (the correction adds 1103 and 1104).
2. 351.202(d) heading and lead-in: proposed 'Employees excluded. The provisions of this part do not apply to the following categories of employees'; final 'Employees excluded from reduction in force competition. An employee holding one of the following appointments is not a competing employee'.
3. 351.202(d)(1)(ii), (2)(i) and (2)(ii): the proposed phrases 'as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice' are removed in the final.
4. 351.202(d)(2)(iii): proposed 'temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316'; final 'temporary appointment of one (1) year or less under subpart D of part 316'.
5. 351.202(d)(3): proposed said such employees may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned 'without regard to the provisions of this part'; final limits this to not determining retention standing (subparts D, E), order of release (F) or assignment rights (G), provided the action is consistent with the appointment and law.
6. 351.202(d)(4): new in the final (written notice with specified content when such an employee is furloughed over 30 days, separated, demoted or reassigned, unless the action is mere expiration).
7. 351.203 'Furlough': the proposed ending 'and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action' is removed.
8. 351.203 'Rating of record': proposed pattern cite 'Sec. 430.208(d)', 'assessing performance'; final 'Sec. 430.208(e)', 'for performance of agency-assigned duties'.
9. 351.203 new definition 'Restoration protected employee' in the final only.
10. 351.203 'Initial probationary period', 'Trial period', 'Military spouse': proposed 'of this chapter'; final as published 'of this part' (initial probationary, trial) and no 'of this chapter' (military spouse), restored to 'of this chapter' by 2026-17335.
11. 351.204: the final adds 'and for ensuring that such regulations are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles set forth in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b)'.
12. 351.302(d): proposed 'adverse action procedures found in part 752 of this chapter'; final 'part 752, if applicable, or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee's appointment'.
13. 351.402: the proposed rule revised only (b); the final also adds (c) (OPM approval of a competitive area established or materially modified within 90 days before notices).
14. 351.502(a)(2)-(3) and (b)(2)-(3): 'as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice' becomes 'as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice'. 351.502(a)(3): 'subpart C or D of part 316' becomes 'subpart D of part 316'.
15. 351.503(a)(1): cross-reference '430.208(d)' becomes '430.208(e)'; 'Minimally Successful' becomes 'Minimally Satisfactory'. 351.503(d) and (e)(1): '430.208(d)' becomes '430.208(e)'. 351.503(d) and (e)(2) add 'authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521'. 351.503(b)(3): 'equivalent ratings of record' becomes 'equivalent to ratings of record'.
16. 351.504(a)(1)-(3): proposed 'should be identified' as Subgroup AD/A/B; final 'must be identified'.
17. 351.505(b)(2): proposed 'covered by Sec. 351.503(b)'; final 'Sec. 351.504(b)'.
18. 351.506(c)(1): proposed 'their performance credit ... their service computation dates'; final 'the employee's performance credit ... the employee's service computation date'. 351.506(d): final adds 'This paragraph does not limit any right of access available under another statute or regulation.' 351.506(c)(2): proposed 'under Sec. 351.701(b) and (c)'; final as published identical, but the correction changed it to '351.701(b)'.
19. 351.507(b): 'under any of this paragraph (b)' becomes 'under any of these provisions'.
20. 351.604: the proposed rule revised (b) and removed (d); the final makes no 351.604 change.
21. 351.605: restructured and expanded. Proposed (a) 'may use this paragraph (a)', (b) with notice content inside it, and 'may not apply assignment rights'. Final has (a) 'this provision', (b), a separate (c) Notice that must identify the competitive area and state the employee was not ranked, and (d) 'must not apply assignment rights', with no retention register required.
22. 351.606(a): proposed one sentence giving 'retention priorities' to employees entitled 'under Sec. 351.209(b)'; final (a)(1)-(6) replaces it, with a mandatory exception applied after ordinary standing, covering Sec. 351.605, citing 'Sec. 353.209(b)' (a changed section cross-reference).
23. 351.608(a)(2): the CTAP cross-reference 'part 330, subpart E' becomes 'part 330, subpart F'.
24. 351.701: the final adds paragraph headings '(a) General' and '(b) Assignment rights'; the Level 2 label changes from 'minimally successful' to 'minimally satisfactory'.
25. 351.702(a)(4)(iii): proposed 'Does not solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination'; final 'Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment'. The final adds (a)(4)(v), the exemption from assessment where the employee in the preceding 5 years held the same (or same-grade, substantially same) position with a rating of Level 3 or higher.
26. 351.802(a): the final adds the introductory phrase 'Except as otherwise provided in this part'. (a)(2): proposed 'veteran status' becomes 'veterans' preference subgroup'. (a)(3): proposed 'access to the agency's records' becomes 'information on how to access the agency's records'.
27. 351.805(b): not amended in the proposal; the final adds the amended-notice rule (a notice solely stating a later effective date is not a new notice for 351.507 and does not require recalculation).
Q11.uncertainty: I compared the part 351 amendments only (not parts 316, 330, 353, 359, 362, 430). The proposal's 351.801-series and 351.603 text was not printed in either. I may have missed minor wording changes within paragraphs I skimmed (351.608(c)-(g), 351.701(c)-(g) read as identical in substance). Items 9 and 11 and 10 involve rules and corrections that interact.

Q12.answer:
Notices were issued Oct. 5, 2026 (after Sept. 2), so the amended rules apply. There is no cutoff date, so the ratings period is Oct. 5, 2022 to Oct. 5, 2026, and the last three ratings in it count.
(a) Register, GS-13 level (tenure group is competitive service):
- Alvarez: 7+7+5 = 19; no preference; total 19; SCD Apr. 4, 2011.
- Chen: Her Sept. 30, 2022 Level 2 is before Oct. 5, 2022, so outside the period. She has two ratings: 7 (Level 5) and 5 (Level 4); proxy (7+5)/2 = 6; credit 7+5+6 = 18; no preference; total 18; subgroup I; SCD May 22, 2017.
- Dube: two ratings (5+5); proxy (5+5)/2 = 5; credit 15; preference eligible, no disability, +3; total 18; subgroup II (career-conditional, probation done); SCD Aug. 3, 2015.
- Estrada: the Oct. 20, 2026 Level 5 was received after the Oct. 5 notice and cannot be used. Ratings used: 5 (Nov. 2023), 3 (Nov. 2024), 5 (Nov. 2025) = 13; +3 preference; total 16; SCD Feb. 6, 2012.
- Brandt: 3+5+0 = 8; +5 (30% disabled, Subgroup AD); total 13.
- Farouk: one rating (Level 3), so 3 x 3 = 9; no preference; total 9. He is a restoration protected employee (351.203): restored under part 353 on July 13, 2026 after 14 months of uniformed service, so he is entitled under 353.209(b) to 6 months or 1 year of retention after restoration. He is protected on Oct. 5 and through the Dec. 4 effective date on either period.
- Quinn: not on the register. A career-conditional employee still in her initial probationary period (appointed Mar. 2, 2026) is not a competing employee (351.202(d)(2)(ii)); she is not ranked.
Order of retention: Alvarez 19, Chen 18, Dube 18, Estrada 16, Brandt 13, Farouk 9. Chen and Dube tie at 18, so tenure subgroup decides (I ahead of II): Chen ahead of Dube, even though Dube's SCD is earlier.
(b) Quinn stays, leaving the six competing employees; three must be released. The three lowest are Farouk, Brandt and Estrada, but Farouk cannot be released while another competing employee can be (351.606(a)(2), mandatory exception applied after ordinary standing). So released are Brandt (13), Estrada (16) and Dube (18, the next lowest). Farouk, Chen and Alvarez stay. Each release is the lowest-standing employee who may be released.
(c) Assignment (351.701): the position must be held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group, within three grades (five for Brandt), and the employee must be qualified. The other holders' standing: Gomez 7+5+5 = 17; Hill 5+3+3 = 11 +3 = 14; Jones 5+5+5 = 15; Ikeda 3+3+3 = 9.
- Dube (18): Gomez (17), Hill (14), Jones (15) are all lower; the least reduction is the GS-12, so the agency must offer Gomez's GS-12. Ikeda's GS-9 is also lower but four grades down.
- Estrada (16): Gomez (17) is higher, so not available. Hill (14) and Jones (15) are lower; the least reduction is the GS-11. The agency must offer Hill's GS-11. Ikeda's GS-9 is beyond three grades.
- Brandt (13, 30% disabled preference eligible; five-grade limit): Gomez 17, Hill 14 and Jones 15 are higher. Only Ikeda (9) is lower. The agency must offer Ikeda's GS-9 (four grades below, within five).
(d) If every offer is accepted, those displaced are Gomez (by Dube), Hill (by Estrada) and Ikeda (by Brandt). The scenario says each is qualified only for the position he or she holds, so none has an assignment right to any other position. Gomez, Hill and Ikeda are separated from the agency. Jones keeps GS-10. Alvarez, Chen, Farouk and Quinn remain at GS-13, with Dube at GS-12, Estrada at GS-11 and Brandt at GS-9.
Q12.uncertainty: 353.209(b) is not printed in these documents (only 353.209(a) is revised), so the 6-month v. 1-year period for Farouk is not established from the Federal Register; the result is the same either way here. The text does not say how the assignment rights order is resolved if several released employees want the same position (not needed here). Hill's and Gomez's standing was computed with the same performance rules; the scenario gives no other ratings.

Q13.answer:
Differences I found between statements in the preamble of 2026-15665 and the regulatory text printed in the same document:
1. Competitive-area safeguard, 'review' v. 'approval'. Preamble (Exec. Summary, 91 FR 49179, 'Providing additional competitive area safeguards'): OPM 'is requiring that, when a competitive area will be in effect less than 90 days prior to a specific RIF notice, or has been materially modified, an agency must submit a description ... and provide, for OPM review, a written explanation'. Text, 351.402(c) (49220): the agency 'shall submit' the description and statement 'to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force'. Other preamble passages state it correctly: 91 FR 49203 ('the requirement in Sec. 351.402(c) that OPM approve new or substantially modified competitive areas') and 91 FR 49196 ('seeking approval from OPM').
2. Competitive-area trigger. Preamble at 91 FR 49196 (limits on 'new competitive areas that will be in effect for less than 90 days before issuance of RIF notices') and 91 FR 49214 ('a proposed competitive area that will be in effect less than 90 days before issuance') omit modification. Text, 351.402(c): 'establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific reduction in force notices'. The Exec. Summary (49179) and 91 FR 49203 correctly mention material modification.
3. Erosion-of-duties paragraph. Preamble at 91 FR 49190 says OPM 'is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove' erosion-of-duties reclassifications. The reclassification exemption and its safeguard are in 351.202(c)(3) (91 FR 49218), whereas 351.201(a)(2) just lists the actions covered. The preamble's description of the safeguard elsewhere on the same page (bars reclassification 'between the formal announcement and completion of a RIF', 91 FR 49190, and Exec. Summary item 8 at 49178) matches the text; the 180-day language at 49190 describes the old rule's trigger.
4. Notice content on records access. Preamble at 91 FR 49205 and 49191 says notices must give 'a link to 5 CFR part 351 and access to the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force'. Text, 351.802(a)(3) (49226): 'A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency's records pertinent to the reduction in force'. I found no preamble passage stating the text's wording.
I did not find further clear mismatches in the limited portions of the 6,000-line document I could search.
Q13.uncertainty: I could not read the whole preamble within the budget and searched by keyword, so this list is incomplete. Item 3 depends on the unprinted current 351.201(a)(2) (351.201(a)(2) is printed as revised and may indeed no longer list erosion of duties). Items 1 and 2 are drawn from separate summary sentences; the regulatory text controls.

Q14.answer:
All items below are checked against the cited text. The final appeals rule is 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230), as corrected by 2026-17338; the proposal is 2026-02576 (91 FR 5861, text at 5874-77); the Board's rule is 2026-16456 (91 FR 51997).
(i) Preamble v. regulatory text (published or corrected):
1. 351.901(b)(1). Preamble (91 FR 49248): the appellant must prove 'that the written appeal was timely and in the required form'. Text (49263): 'The timeliness of the written appeal', with nothing about form.
2. 351.901(c)(1). Preamble (49248): 'the procedures in part 351 are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action'. Text as published (49263): 'The procedures in this part'; as corrected by 2026-17338: 'The procedures in this subpart'.
3. Existing collective bargaining agreements. Preamble (91 FR 49244-45): the rule 'does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs', does not 'automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term', and 'when agreements are renegotiated' the rule will limit the duty and ability to bargain. Text 351.901(c)(2) (49263-64): RIF actions and appeal matters 'may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration', for covered RIFs from Sept. 2, with no renegotiation condition.
4. Judicial review. Preamble (91 FR 49242-43): the rule 'does not withdraw judicial review that Congress provided'. Text 351.901(c)(4) (49264): 'A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart'; 351.909(e): no further right of appeal.
5. 351.904(c). Preamble (49250) says 'OPM or the responsible agency may disallow'. As corrected, the text says 'the agency whose action is under appeal', because 'responsible agency' is undefined in part 351.
(ii) Changes from proposal to final not acknowledged in the final rule's summary of changes (91 FR 49230-32):
1. 351.901(c)(3): the proposal listed the Federal Labor Relations Authority among the entities whose matters are preserved (5874-75); the final drops FLRA (49264). The summary lists EEOC, IGs, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC without saying FLRA was removed.
2. 351.903(b)(1): the proposal said the agency response is due 'within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal' (5875); the final says 'within 30 calendar days after service of the initial appeal' (49264).
3. 351.905(c): the proposal allowed 'a hearing or any other appropriate action' and directed the parties to participate (5876); the final keeps only 'a hearing' (49265-66). The final also adds OPM's power to 'require either party to provide additional information'.
4. 351.902(c)(2): the final adds 'or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause' to the registration requirement (49264).
5. 351.906(b): the proposal said OPM 'shall' impose the listed sanctions (5876); the final says 'may' (49266). The final also adds (c), requiring sanctions to be proportionate and no broader than necessary.
6. 351.909(c): the final adds that an untimely request granted for good cause leads to a decision that becomes final under (b) (49266-67). The authority citation is also expanded (1103, 1104, 2301, 38 U.S.C. 4331).
(iii) The Board's rule (2026-16456) v. OPM's rule and within itself, on which RIF appeals the Board will still hear:
1. Within the Board's rule: DATES (91 FR 51997) says the Board will not apply the rule to pending cases or 'newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken before the effective date'. Section I.B (51997) says it will accept cases 'where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date'. Section III (51998) says it will adjudicate RIF appeals received after Sept. 2 'in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026'. These use three different tests: action date, notice date and RIF effective date.
2. Against OPM's rule: OPM covers a RIF only if notice was issued on or after Sept. 2 (91 FR 49230); notices before then stay with MSPB (49248). The Board's Section III test (effective date before Sept. 2) would leave a RIF with notice before Sept. 2 and an effective date on or after Sept. 2 (for example, notice Aug. 31, effective Oct. 30) outside both OPM's process and the Board's stated rule. The Board's own notice-date sentence (51997) does match OPM's.
Q14.uncertainty: I did not compare every sentence of the long preamble with the text; the lists are those I verified. (i)(5) is a terminology difference. (i)(4) is a difference in characterization rather than a contradiction of text. (ii) lists only changes I confirmed by comparing the two texts side by side, and the summary does acknowledge many others.
